Climate & Environment
• UN climate summit COP31 collapsed without a final deal for the first time since 2009 amid rifts over fossil fuels and climate finance, prompting calls to reform UN decision rules.
• NGOs warn of severe environmental degradation: Oxfam says Gaza shows signs of widespread contamination, while scientists report lasting damage to Australian coastal wetlands from the 2019–20 bushfires.
• New analyses urge climate-proofed infrastructure planning to avoid trillions in wasted investment, and question the global use of US soil-erosion models in the Global South.
• Emerging tech and policy debates: enhanced rock weathering for carbon removal may depress crop yields over time; California braces for king tides and floods; research suggests plant-based lunches could cut Australia’s emissions by 15m tonnes annually.
Why it matters: The failure at COP31 underscores widening fractures over fossil fuels and funding, raising stakes for climate resilience, justice, and near-term action.

Climate & Environment.text: Rain and wind erode fertile soil worldwide. The topsoil, where plants take root and where most of the nutrients are found, is washed away from fields by heavy rain, particularly on slopes and where the ground is not covered by vegetation. Entertainment.title: TOMORROW X TOGETHER Find Upheaval Worth Running Toward on 'PERFECT STORM'
Entertainment.text: A line in "Angel Bite" is "Even love costs money," and it's about as blunt as TOMORROW X TOGETHER have ever been. Taehyun says that's on purpose. Over the years, the group has written different versions of this song, penning metaphors to express what it's like to hold on to someone you have nothing to give. This time around, he says they wanted to "strip down all the romanticized notions of youth and actually confront the anxiety, pain, and sense of deprivation underneath it." Another line on the song pushes it further: "Ain't got nothing, so how am I supposed to afford a future?"The intentionality runs across the entirety of PERFECT STORM. Their latest project arrives only only seven months after 7TH YEAR: A Moment of Stillness in the Thorns, and shifts the focus from 7TH YEAR's anxieties to what they did next. "For us, a storm isn't an obstacle to fight against, but a catalyst for change that sweeps away the stagnant air and opens doors to new possibilities," Taehyun explains. "We definitely felt the need for change, and this album is our way of diving headfirst into that whirlwind of transformation."Soobin reveals the storm wasn't the plan from the start. When they first sat down, the only thing everyone agreed on was that they needed to do "something completely different" from what they've done before. The storm idea came later, as they worked it through with their team. What he talks about more is what happened once they started writing. "In the beginning, all the anxieties we had felt massive and uncontrollable, almost like we were bracing ourselves for an approaching storm. But after writing our thoughts and feelings into the lyrics and vocalizing it, everything started to feel a lot more manageable." The concept photos follow that change fairly literally, taking the members from waiting for the storm to riding it, standing in its eye and finally holding it in their hands. "Now, I can say that we are getting closer to truly embracing the storm, just like in our last concept photos, 'HOLDING THE STORM.'"The music doesn't stay in one place either, moving through dance punk, minimal techno and avant-pop over the course of the album. Ask whether there's a point where it stops sounding like them, and Hueningkai doesn't really accept the premise. "We don't really draw a line or set rules on what sounds like us. When we're working on music, our main priority is pushing past our comfort zones and trying new things. We want to keep growing and constantly surprise MOA with something that feels fresh every time."The unit tracks shuffle the lineup the same way. "Sweetest Escape" hears Yeonjun, Taehyun and Hueningkai together, and "Touch the Sky" pairs Soobin with Beomgyu - two members who had never recorded a unit track together. "Our vocal tones and approaches are quite different, but hearing the track come together, I think our individual styles really shined through!" Beomgyu shares. Having only two voices filling a track cost them time, but both Beomgyu and Soobin are immensely proud of how it turned out."Higher Love" deals with ambition, and it's the kind that hurts but also keeps you going. That's a fair thing to ask a group with eight Top 5 albums on the Billboard 200 and a Lollapalooza headlining set behind them about. "The hunger to go higher is definitely still there, but pointed in a slightly different direction," Yeonjun says. "In our early debut days, we wanted to prove to the world who we are, which often led to feeling pressure on our shoulders. Now, we're learning to embrace that pressure while maintaining an uncompromising pride in our work."They'll be taking that into two very different kinds of show. "STEAL THE WIND," their fifth world tour, is about to begin, and in December they make their Jingle Ball debut in front of crowds where plenty of people will be seeing them for the first time. Yeonjun says they build each set around who's in the room. The tour gets the biggest hits alongside fan-favorite B-sides and unit stages. For Jingle Ball, "we try to catch their attention from the first beat by showing our absolute highlights."PERFECT STORM ends on "Hate It or Love It," a poignant song about having the courage to leave the familiar behind. After creating an album that is so focused on what things cost, it feels like the right place to stop. If love costs money, growing up costs comfort, and for at least one member, this comeback came at the price of his favorite midnight delivery order.The album ends with "Hate It or Love It. "What's something comfortable you've had to walk away from to keep growing, as a group or individually?SOOBIN: Late-night snacks. I know this sounds pretty minor, but ordering our favorite delivery food in the middle of the night was always our little happiness. But to get ready for this comeback, we dialed back a little on that guilty pleasure so we could show up for MOA at our absolute best!"Angel Bite" has playful, game-inspired sounds in it. If PERFECT STORM were a video game, what genre is it? And who's the player who finds every hidden secret, and who rage-quits first?BEOMGYU: That's an interesting question. If PERFECT STORM were a video game, I think it would be a narrative-driven action game. You know, the type of game with intense battles and dramatic twists. Soobin is actually good at finding hidden clues. He has a sharp eye for details. As for rage-quitting, none of us really get angry like that, though we do have someone who will quietly shut down his computer and lie face-down in his pillow. He'd get embarrassed if I tell who that is, so I won't tell who!You're stuck in an actual storm, say the tour bus breaks down on the way to a show. Who panics, who makes the plan, who falls asleep, and who's quietly filming everything?HUENINGKAI: That's definitely a situation I wouldn't want to end up in! Taehyun is the realist of our group, so I think he is going to be the one who comes up with a plan to get us out of there, while SOOBIN would make sure we all stay calm. Yeonjun and Beomgyu would probably start cracking jokes to lighten the mood, and I'd be laughing along with them.To close, a "Hate It or Love It" lightning round. We'll throw out everyday things and each of you has to pick a side, no "it depends" allowed. Rainy days?SOOBIN: HateYEONJUN: HateBEOMGYU: LoveTAEHYUN: LoveHUENINGKAI: LoveMint chocolate?SOOBIN: HateYEONJUN: LoveBEOMGYU: HateTAEHYUN: HateHUENINGKAI: Love6 a.m. flights?SOOBIN: HateYEONJUN: HateBEOMGYU: HateTAEHYUN: HateHUENINGKAI: HateKaraoke?SOOBIN: HateYEONJUN: LoveBEOMGYU: HateTAEHYUN: LoveHUENINGKAI: HateSpicy food?SOOBIN: HateYEONJUN: LoveBEOMGYU: LoveTAEHYUN: HateHUENINGKAI: HateGroup chats?SOOBIN: LoveYEONJUN: LoveBEOMGYU: HateTAEHYUN: HateHUENINGKAI: LoveClick here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Entertainment.title: American Airlines and Alpha Industries Reimagine the MA-1 Flight Jacket for Airline’s 100th Anniversary
Entertainment.text: American Airlines has teamed up with Alpha Industries to celebrate its 100th anniversary with a limited-edition MA-1 Flight Jacket, transforming leather reclaimed from retired aircraft seats into a wearable piece of aviation history.Spearheaded by creative agency Ceeze, the collaboration brings together American Airlines’ archival heritage and Alpha Industries’ iconic MA-1 silhouette. Rather than relying on conventional fabrics, the project repurposes authentic upholstery from American Airlines’ retired fleet. Each jacket is handcrafted in New York City, with the reclaimed leather carefully cut, rearranged and reconstructed into a distinctive patchwork design. Only 100 pieces will be produced worldwide.Design-wise, the jacket features a dark blue leather exterior complemented by a red satin lining, silver zipper and graphite-colored ribbed cuffs. An American Airlines logo patch dating back to the 1930s completes the design, paying homage to the airline’s century-long history.Originally developed as functional military outerwear, the MA-1 Flight Jacket has since transcended its utilitarian origins, becoming a staple across youth subcultures, streetwear and high fashion. This latest collaboration reconnects the silhouette with its aviation roots, giving authentic aircraft materials a second life while offering a fresh interpretation of an enduring wardrobe icon.The American Airlines x Alpha Industries 100th Anniversary MA-1 Flight Jacket has officially been unveiled, with further release details yet to be announced.Of the 100 jackets made, American Airlines plans to make 50 available to AAdvantage® members through AAdvantage Exchange for 200,000 AAdvantage® miles each. Entertainment.title: Palace Skateboards Unveils Holiday 2026 Lookbook
Entertainment.text: SummaryPalace's Holiday 2026 lookbook is mostly cold-weather outerwear, with WINDSTOPPER by GORE-TEX LABS sets, quilted puffers, flight-style parkas and heavy sherpa fleeceThe knitwear includes Fair Isle snowflake bands, rose intarsia zip hoodies and a crewneck with three fawns across the chestA fawn print, a halftone skull print and classical statue artwork repeat across jackets, shirts, denim and headwearPalace Skateboards has released the lookbook for its Holiday 2026 collection, a heavily layered lineup built around insulation, technical shells and textured knits for the coldest months of the year. The first drop of the season covers outerwear, fleece, knitwear, denim, sweats and headwear. Throughout, Palace mixes trail- and military-inspired construction with some of its most playful graphics of the year.The most technical pieces are a set of hooded jackets and matching pants carrying WINDSTOPPER by GORE-TEX LABS branding down the sleeve and leg. Both run in a pale grey version with red hits and a black version printed with tonal halftone skulls and yellow branding. Contrast piping traces the shoulders and the outer seams of the pants, and the jackets add a drawcord hood, elastic cuffs, a cinched hem and taped-look zip pockets alongside a Tri-Ferg on the chest.The insulated outerwear covers several silhouettes. A navy ripstop puffer is blocked in two tones with a small oval logo, and a cropped green ripstop version is covered in a fawn-and-butterfly print. There's also a burgundy hooded puffer with a gold "PALACE" arch across the chest and gold-and-cream striped rib cuffs and hem. A black leather puffer is quilted in chevron channels with an elastic hem and a brown pile collar. Flight-style parkas in navy and sage add button-through plackets, a utility sleeve pocket, rib-knit hems and a hood with a shaggy white trim.Fleece takes up a large part of the collection. Sand sherpa zip jackets are paneled with green woven trim on the collar and chest flap pockets, which carry a Tri-Ferg patch, and the back shows a chenille oval-logo patch. Two hooded sherpa zips in forest green and cream are knitted through with Fair Isle snowflakes and zigzag bands. Lighter fleece shows up in an olive hooded zip with neon yellow zippers and a tonal sleeve logo, a grey half-zip striped in coral with an embossed "Palace" triangle logo, and a navy fleece rugby shirt with a white woven collar.The knitwear is where the graphics are most detailed. Chunky zip hoodies in pink and black carry intarsia roses on the chest, and the black version adds a large back panel with a haloed figure, a dove, a cluster of roses and a script "Palace." A navy crewneck repeats the Fair Isle snowflake bands under a blocky white wordmark, and a black crewneck has three fawns knitted across the chest.The prints carry over into the rest of the collection. The fawn motif reappears on a white button-down Oxford shirt and a fuzzy beanie with bear ears. The halftone skull covers a thermal long sleeve, track pants and a balaclava. A purple classical statue print appears on a denim trucker jacket, matching jeans and a mesh V-neck jersey. Other graphic pieces include a gothic "Skull Crusher" zip hoodie and matching orange T-shirt, a caroler-themed Tri-Ferg T-shirt, a woodland camo hoodie and a Tri-Ferg T-shirt with a liquid-bubble graphic. Houndstooth shirt jackets, collegiate "PAL ACE" arch sweats, trapper caps with plush ear flaps and a faux fur leopard hat fill out the collection.The first Holiday 2026 drop from Palace launches Friday, November 27 at 11 a.m. in the UK, Europe and the US, then Saturday, November 28 at 11 a.m. local time in Japan, Singapore, China, Korea and Australia.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Entertainment.title: SR_A Unveils New GRIND Editorial Collection
Entertainment.text: SR_A recently unveiled its new GRIND Editorial collection, which centers on traditional indigo dyeing techniques to combine functional fabrics, natural silk, and retro sportswear. Through manual dyeing, fading, and distressing treatments, the collection presents clothing pieces that boast both utilitarian attributes and unique textures.This collection includes items such as parkas, jackets, zip hoodies, and tracksuits. After garment construction, all pieces undergo a 72-hour handmade indigo dyeing process, allowing different materials to display natural color variations and textural depth.In outerwear, the BONDED GARNET INDIGO SILK PARKA and SILENT FOREST INDIGO SILK PARKA are crafted from Italian Limonta water-repellent functional fabric and matte gabardine, respectively. They feature natural raw silk from Jaipur, India, vintage brass hardware, and vegetable-tanned leather brim details incorporating Japanese Sashiko embroidery, forging a connection between modern outdoor functionality and traditional craftsmanship. The BRONZE TINT INDIGO SILK JACKET uses crinkled raw silk as its main fabric, combined with a high-collar design and satin lining to present a more fluid silhouette. The CERU INDIGO SHELL PARKA opts for lightweight pure cotton fabric and adds adjustable webbing and vintage prints, emphasizing the practicality of outdoor wear.For sportswear, the collection brings the AQUA, MARINE, and WOODLAND INDIGO ZIP HOODIES, as well as the VIOLET INDIGO RAGLAN top. The designs carry on the cropped proportions and dropped shoulders of retro sportswear, imparting varying degrees of wear marks through high-temperature plastisol printing, bleaching, sun-fading, and localized distress treatments. Notably, the MARINE version specifically utilizes waffle cotton fabric, paired with a more tailored athletic silhouette.Additionally, the TREATED INDIGO 1/4 PULLOVER and TREATED INDIGO ZIP JOGGER are based on classic tracksuits, utilizing brushed, high-density pure cotton fabric. They combine understated water-based distressed prints, zippered pockets, and a quarter-zip high collar structure, integrating more functional details into the retro athletic style.From Italian functional fabrics and Indian raw silk to traditional Japanese handcrafts, SR_A re-explores the relationship between modern apparel and traditional manufacturing methods through a combination of different materials and techniques. The handmade dyeing and distressed treatments in the collection also ensure that each piece presents its own unique color and texture.SR_A's new GRIND Editorial collection has now officially debuted, with specific release information yet to be announced.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Entertainment.text: SummaryAction Bronson was spotted courtside wearing a bespoke championship-inspired ring by Gerard Alexander of Saint JewelsThe one-of-one piece celebrates the New York Knicks' 2026 title and the end of the franchise's 53-year championship droughtThe intricate design features a miniature Madison Square Garden concealed under the top and can also be worn as a pendantCelebrated rapper, chef, and New York native Action Bronson stepped out courtside last night wearing a one-of-a-kind bespoke Saint Jewels New York Knicks 2026 Title Ring. Entertainment.title: Jeff Staple Announces the Closure of Staple 21 Mercer in New York City
Entertainment.text: SummaryJeff Staple is officially closing his Staple 21 Mercer retail space in New York City after a 20-month runThe SoHo location served as a community-driven gathering place for music, art, sports, gaming, and entrepreneurshipStaple plans to pivot away from a permanent flagship in favor of pop-ups and experiential retail activations around the cityJeff Staple has officially announced the closure of his Staple 21 Mercer retail store in New York City. Taking over the former NikeLab space in SoHo, the destination operated as a vibrant retail and cultural hub for 20 months, with its final day of operation officially set for Friday, November 27.Reflecting on the space's tenure, the brand emphasized that the location was always intended to be more than just a traditional retail storefront. Built as a cultural gathering place where community came before commerce, Staple 21 Mercer frequently welcomed creatives and innovators across the spheres of music, art, sports, and gaming. The brand's founder noted that the most memorable moments of the store's run were entirely unplanned, capturing the serendipitous spirit of New York City. Employees similarly echoed the sentiment, expressing gratitude for the connections built and legends met during the store's operations.While the physical address is shutting its doors, the Staple brand and its iconic Pigeon logo are shifting strategies rather than slowing down. The label plans to transition away from a permanent seven-days-a-week flagship model in favor of dynamic pop-ups, retail experiments, and global activations. This pivot aims to ensure that every future physical brand experience feels more intentional and impactful for the community.Staple 21 Mercer will remain open for one final stretch, inviting fans to shop and share memories before officially closing its doors on Black Friday, November 27.
